title: Spatiotemporal remodeling in habenula marks the onset of depression-related phenotypes
title_zh: 海马旁核的时空重塑标志着抑郁相关表型的出现
abstract: Abstract Chronic stress has lasting adverse consequences that can lead, over time, to depression, yet the optimal timeframe for effective therapies remains unclear. The lateral habenula (LHb) has been implicated in stress-related behavioral repercussions, but the precise timing of its contribution is not understood. Here, using spatial transcriptomics, we generated a spatially resolved molecular atlas of the LHb of male mice, revealing a topographically organized and temporally defined remodeling of gene expression after chronic stress. Longitudinal in vivo two-photon calcium imaging of individual LHb neurons revealed progressively heightened excitatory responses to aversive stimuli. These neuronal adaptations mirrored both the progression of transcriptional changes and the emergence of depression-related behavioral phenotypes and were reversed by the antidepressant ketamine. Moreover, chemogenetically limiting LHb neuronal activity or administering ketamine at the onset of these changes exerted antidepressant effects. These findings link spatiotemporal signatures of LHb neuronal ensembles and genetic landscape with the onset of stress-induced depression-related states.
abstract_zh: 摘要：慢性压力具有持久的不良后果，随着时间的推移可能导致抑郁，但有效治疗的最佳时机尚不清楚。侧海马旁核（LHb）已被认为与压力相关的行为后果有关，但其贡献的精确时机尚未明了。本文利用空间转录组学生成了雄性小鼠LHb的空间分辨分子图谱，揭示了慢性压力后基因表达的拓扑组织和时间定义的重塑。对单个LHb神经元进行纵向体内双光子钙成像显示，对厌恶刺激的兴奋性反应逐步增强。这些神经元适应与转录变化的进展以及抑郁相关行为表型的出现相对应，并可被抗抑郁药氯胺酮逆转。此外，化学遗传学限制LHb神经元活动或在这些变化开始时给药氯胺酮均具有抗抑郁作用。这些发现将LHb神经元集群的时空特征与遗传景观与压力诱导的抑郁相关状态的出现联系起来。
